seo.metaDescription: Hurt in a fall in Wasco? Get a free case review from an attorney who handles premises liability claims. No fee unless you recover.

hero.subtitle: A fall on someone else's property in Wasco can leave you with medical bills and unanswered questions about who's responsible. We can review what happened at the store, sidewalk, or business where you were hurt and explain your legal options.

about.title: Wasco Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Wasco property owners, from businesses along F Street and Palm Avenue to farm-adjacent lots near Rt 46 and Rt 43, are expected to keep their premises reasonably safe for visitors. When a spill, broken pavement, poor lighting, or a hidden hazard causes a fall, California law generally requires the injured person to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the danger and failed to address it in time. That's why documentation matters so much here: photos of the hazard, names of witnesses, and any store or building surveillance footage can make the difference in a claim. Our team handles premises liability claims on a contingency basis, so there's no upfront cost to you. We can evaluate the property owner's conduct and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises law hinges on notice — we can help gather records, inspection logs, or witness statements showing the property owner had time to fix or warn about the hazard.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Before It's Erased
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks, so acting quickly to request preservation of video can be critical to supporting your account of the fall.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: Because California applies pure comparative fault, even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount — we can explain how that could apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Wasco?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a claim, though claims against a public entity, such as a city building or park, often have a much shorter notice deadline. It's best to have an attorney review your situation as soon as possible so deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: What if I fell at a business off Rt 46 or Palm Avenue and no one saw it happen?
items.answer: Even without witnesses, evidence like photos of the hazard, your clothing or shoes, incident reports, and store surveillance video can help establish what happened. We can advise you on what to collect and how to request footage before it's deleted.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to get help?
items.answer: No. Our consultations are free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
